AMERICAN SYSTEMS is hiring a Java Developer I to help develop Java applications and data integration solutions in a high-volume, low-latency environment. The role supports the software development life cycle, troubleshooting, testing, releases, and collaboration with senior team members.
Government
Information Technology

Responsibilities
Develop and maintain Java-based applications and TIBCO integrations in a high-volume, low-latency environment
Troubleshoot real-time system issues and provide timely support
Participate in all stages of the SDLC, including design, development, testing, and deployment
Implement unit tests and automated tests to ensure code quality
Apply Object-Oriented Programming (OOP) principles and standard design patterns
Work with web services, REST APIs, and technologies like XML, JSON, and HTML
Use version control tools (e.g., Git) and build tools (e.g., Ant, Maven, Gradle)
Collaborate with teams to gather requirements and define business processes
Adhere to Agile methodologies and participate in team activities (e.g., sprints)
Support software releases and contribute to continuous improvement processes

Required
* Bachelor's degree in computer science or related
* 0-2 years of hands-on experience in Java development
As a requirement of this position, all candidates must be a U.S. Citizen
* Knowledge of Java programming and Object-Oriented Programming (OOP) principles
* Familiarity with TIBCO systems or a strong willingness to learn
* Exposure to web services (REST, XML, JSON) and web technologies like HTML
* Experience with code versioning tools such as Git (academic or project work counts)
* Basic understanding of Agile methodologies (e.g., sprints, daily stand-ups)
* Familiarity with cloud platforms such as AWS or Azure (willingness to learn if no prior experience)
* Strong problem-solving skills with a focus on debugging and troubleshooting
* Ability to work collaboratively in a team environment and follow guidance from senior developers
* Eagerness to learn and grow with new technologies, tools, and best practices
